newsitem.title: USA: GM union in Ohio sees early contract deal.
newsitem.headline: GM union in Ohio sees early contract deal.

text.p: An officer of a union representing 4,100 workers at a General Motors Corp assembly plant in Moraine, Ohio, on Monday said the union had withdrawn a strike notice.
The union notified GM last week that it would strike at 0001 EST/0501 GMT Tuesday if progress was not made in negotiations over a new three-year contract.

"We have some language we need to work out (but) we continue to negotiate," Willie Thorpe, president of Local 801 of the International Union of Electronic Workers, told Reuters. "I think we can work this out."
He said the strike notice could be reissued if necessary.
A GM spokesman could not immediately be reached. Earlier the automaker said it was confident an agreement could be reached. GM declined last week to discuss the specific issues involved in the talks.
The plant, near Dayton, assembles Chevrolet Blazer, GMC Jimmy and Olsmobile Bravada sport utility vehicles.
